subject: sr-business-studies
title: Co-ordination and Controlling
meta: Lesson practice set · Question types of the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: Practice set for this lesson in the question types of the April 2026 paper.
Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

questions.q: The first step in the controlling process is —
questions.answer: B

questions.q: Co-ordination is called the —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Controlling looks back at ______ performance and forward to ______ performance.
questions.answer: A

questions.q: A factory manager compares daily production with the daily target. This illustrates the ______ function.
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which function ensures the right timing and sequence of activities?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which function ensures that activities conform to the plans?
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of controlling?
options: It is a lower-level function only
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Corrective action is required only for deviations —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: The importance of co-ordination is —
questions.answer: A

questions.q: Who defined control as 'verifying whether everything occurs in conformity with the plan adopted'?
questions.answer: A

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (a) Control looks back at ______ performance. (b) Control looks forward to ______ performance.
questions.answer: (a) past. (b) future.

questions.q: Identify the management function: (a) Ensures the right timing and sequence of activities. (b) Ensures that activities conform to the plans.
questions.answer: (a) Co-ordination. (b) Controlling.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Co-ordination leads to diversity in action. (ii) Control is a continuous process.
questions.answer: (i) False – unity of action. (ii) True.

questions.q: Name any two features of control.
questions.answer: It is a continuous process; it is all pervasive and action oriented (any two).

questions.q: Arrange the steps of the control process: comparing actual performance, setting standards, corrective action, measuring performance, finding reasons for deviation.
questions.answer: Setting standards; measuring performance; comparing performance with standards; finding reasons for deviation; corrective action.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: Planning fixes the ______ and controlling checks the ______ performance against them.
questions.answer: standards (goals); actual.

questions.q: State true or false: (i) Without planning control is blind. (ii) Minor deviations within the permissible range need major corrective action.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) False.

questions.q: Name the management function called the 'essence of management'.
questions.answer: Co-ordination.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: A car company's sales team promised early delivery but production could not meet it. Which management function is missing? Mention two problems.
questions.answer: Co-ordination; customer dissatisfaction and a decline in the company's reputation.

questions.q: What is meant by controlling? Name its first step.
questions.answer: Controlling is evaluating actual performance against standards and taking corrective action; first step: establishment of standards.

questions.q: Why is co-ordination called the essence of management?
questions.answer: Because all functions need unity of action and co-ordination ties departments and efforts together to reach common goals.

questions.q: State any two characteristics of co-ordination.
questions.answer: It integrates group efforts and is a continuous and all-pervasive process.

questions.q: How does a deviation within the permissible range get treated?
questions.answer: No corrective action is needed; managers act only on major deviations outside the range.

questions.q: State any two limitations of standards in control.
questions.answer: If too high, employees are discouraged; if too low, efficiency falls and costs rise.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: A factory manager regularly checks the production output and compares it with the daily target. Explain how this illustrates the controlling function.
questions.answer: He measures actual output, compares it with the standard (daily target), finds deviations, ascertains reasons and takes corrective action, which are the steps of controlling.

questions.q: Explain any three points of significance of co-ordination.
questions.answer: It reconciles goals of different departments, avoids overlapping and conflict as size grows and ensures economy and efficiency.

questions.q: Explain any three characteristics of co-ordination.
questions.answer: It integrates group efforts, ensures unity of action and is continuous, all pervasive and the responsibility of all managers.

questions.q: Explain the importance of controlling (any three points).
questions.answer: Helps in achieving targets, takes corrective action on time and improves employee performance.

questions.q: Explain the process of control in three steps (any three).
questions.answer: Setting standards, measuring actual performance and comparing it with standards.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the process of controlling.
questions.answer: Establishing standards, measuring performance, comparing it with standards, detecting reasons for deviations and taking corrective action.

questions.q: Explain the importance of co-ordination and why it is called the essence of management.
questions.answer: As size, location and specialisation increase, co-ordination gives unity of action, reconciles goals and brings efficiency and harmony.

questions.q: Explain why control is needed and its characteristics.
questions.answer: Control helps achieve targets and corrective action on time, improves performance, coordination and planning; it is continuous, all-pervasive, action-oriented and forward looking.
